title: When the Guard Adds Nothing: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for LLM‑Produced Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to measure whether a deterministic generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pipeline increases the probability that an LLM‑produced vendor CLI configuration passes a conservative deterministic validator, relative to direct LLM generation. The preregistered design froze a single shared initial candidate per task (one generator call shared by both arms) and allowed at most one automatic repair call for the guarded arm if the shared initial failed. Using a curated 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest and the declared generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa), every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: baseline = 300/300; guarded = 300/300. The paired contingency table is n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because no initial failures occurred, the preregistered one‑repair policy was never invoked. We release the full preregistration, task manifest, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with canonical SHA‑256 hashes to enable exact reproduction and controlled follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
Generative language models are being proposed to convert high‑level operator intent into vendor CLI configurations to accelerate NetOps. Such proposals must be evaluated in operationally meaningful terms: specifically, whether pipeline designs (generator + validator + bounded repair) materially increase the production of configurations that meet conservative safety invariants before deployment. The generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pattern is widely recommended in tool‑assisted self‑correction literature, but quantitative, artifact‑grounded evidence about the incremental value of a bounded repair stage—holding generator snapshot, prompt, and validator fixed—is sparse.

Research question and contribution. We preregistered (study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e; preregistration SHA‑256 = a85d66d4c6ce2275e2d8c820f96c610532dbb5452bebb3fe108848f9dc38cdf6) and executed a paired experiment asking: under a shared initial candidate per task, does allowing a single automatic repair call (guarded arm) increase the per‑task probability of producing a deterministic‑validator‑passing configuration compared to direct generation (baseline)? Our contributions are: (1) a fully archived preregistration and execution bundle (artifacts and canonical SHA‑256 hashes enumerated in execution/execution_manifest.json), (2) a conservative deterministic validator and a curated 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest frozen prior to model calls (task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3), (3) a confirmatory paired analysis executed exactly as preregistered, and (4) public archival of raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts to enable exact replay (see execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.related_work: Prior work has explored LLM‑assisted intent translation and intent‑based networking (e.g., Nguyen et al., 2024; Chakraborty et al., CNSM 2024) and proposed verifier‑centric guardrails and repair loops in NetOps and database query generation contexts. Studies on tool‑augmented self‑refinement and bounded correction (INTERACSPARQL and related work) influenced our bounded single‑repair policy. Formal verification and deterministic policy checking (Bagpipe / Weitz et al., 2016) shaped our conservative validator design. Unlike broad benchmark papers that measure model ability on open tasks, this experiment isolates an operational property—the marginal value of a bounded repair step given a fixed generator, prompt, and conservative validator—under a preregistered, reproducible contract.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered protocol (study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e; SHA‑256 above) fixed the paired design, analysis plan, stopping rules, seeds, and artifact publishing. Unit of pairing: task. For each task the pipeline produced one shared initial candidate (single generator call). Baseline outcome: validator(initial). Guarded outcome: validator(initial) or, if initial failed, a single automatic repair call and revalidation. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The analysis plan specified an exact McNemar two‑sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Task manifest and deterministic validator. The curated multi‑vendor 300‑task manifest encodes initial network state, operator intent, required safe sequences (e.g., down‑before‑change, make‑before‑break), and expected final state. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) implements conservative checks: CLI parsing/canonicalization, syntactic correctness, interface existence and assignment invariants, workflow invariants (must‑be‑down rules), and destructive‑pattern detection. Validator outputs are structured JSON traces (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb30cb9d03...). The manifest and validator code were frozen and archived before model calls.

Generator, prompts, and execution contract. Declared generator snapshot: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Prompts (generation and repair templates) were frozen and archived. Execution adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution contract permitted at most one repair call per task (if initial failed); in practice the run used one shared initial generation per task (300 generator calls total). All provider traces, cached call artifacts, and raw responses are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ with canonical hashes to enable auditor replay.

Statistical procedures. Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided on the paired 2×2 table (n11, n10, n01, n00). Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for paired difference computed with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729. Prespecified secondary analyses included per‑vendor paired comparisons with Bonferroni correction (family α = 0.05 → per‑comparison α ≈ 0.0167); these are addressed in Results given the observed data.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw outcomes. The run completed exactly as preregistered. Planned episodes = 600 (300 tasks × 2 arms using a shared initial); completed episodes = 600; failed episodes = 0; model_calls_used = 300 (one shared initial per task); repair calls allowed but never invoked (repair_call_count = 0). All artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes are enumerated in execution/execution_manifest.json (example hashes: execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2..., execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558ed...). Representative raw response files (shared initial / baseline / guarded) and scoring JSONs are archived (examples: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be..., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb...).

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). Every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: baseline_success_count = 300/300; guarded_success_count = 300/300. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c94...) is n11 = 300, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because there were no validator failures on the shared initial candidates, the preregistered single repair attempt was not invoked for any task and thus contributed zero additional model calls or passes.

Pre‑specified secondary per‑vendor tests. The preregistration specified per‑vendor paired comparisons. The observed dataset exhibits zero discordant pairs overall; consequently each vendor subgroup also has zero discordant pairs and the per‑vendor McNemar tests are non‑informative under this outcome. The canonical task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 above) contains vendor labels and counts; auditors may re‑slice or replay the run to produce discordance if desired. We therefore report the preregistered per‑vendor analyses as not informative under the observed ceiling (zero discordant pairs), and we provide artifact paths so readers can compute vendor‑level counts directly from the archived manifest.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. The preregistered shared‑initial paired design isolates the marginal value of a bounded repair step applied to the exact same generator output. Under the tested generator snapshot and frozen prompt family, every shared initial candidate already satisfied the conservative validator. In that regime a bounded single repair cannot improve deterministic pass probability because there were no initial failures to repair; the observed paired difference is exactly zero (point estimate and bootstrap CI collapse to 0.00).

Implications for NetOps pipeline design. The null result advises practitioners to empirically measure generator failure rates on their target distribution before deploying bounded repair stages: if generator error rates are near zero, a bounded repair stage adds latency and cost without increasing deterministic‑validator pass rates. Conversely, if a deployment distribution produces validator failures, bounded repair (or expanded repair budgets) may be beneficial; our archive enables controlled follow‑ups under those regimes.

Why the ceiling occurred and reproducible follow‑ups. Three non‑exclusive, artifact‑testable explanations are: (1) the curated manifest difficulty is modest relative to the generator capability given the frozen prompt; (2) prompt scaffolding biased outputs toward validator‑compliant forms; (3) the declared model snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 above) has alignment properties that yield high accuracy on the manifest. These hypotheses are directly testable using the released artifacts: recompose a manifest with higher adversariality, replay with independent (non‑shared) initial draws per arm, permit iterative repair budgets >1, or swap generator snapshot. All raw inputs and traces necessary for such reproducible follow‑ups are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json enumerates artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment asking whether a bounded single automatic repair increases deterministic‑validator pass probability when the same initial LLM candidate is shared by both arms. Under the frozen manifest, prompts, and declared generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini; SHA‑256 listed above), every shared initial passed a conservative deterministic validator and the preregistered single repair stage was never invoked. Observed paired contingency: n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. The evidence is fully archived with canonical SHA‑256 hashes to permit exact reproduction and to support controlled follow‑ups that vary task difficulty, model snapshot, prompt, or repair budget. The empirical lesson is simple and concrete: bounded repair adds value only when generator error rates produce validator failures on the target distribution; otherwise it is operational overhead. All artifacts required for replay and deeper exploration are enumerated in execution/execution_manifest.json.

limitations: Single model snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated — results do not generalize across models or model versions.

Deterministic validator implements a conservative subset of operational hazards (syntactic checks, interface and workflow invariants) and omits dynamic/emulation‑level checks and deeper routing semantics.

Curated 300‑task manifest may omit adversarial or out‑of‑distribution failure modes; under the chosen prompt and model snapshot every shared initial candidate passed the validator (ceiling effect), limiting the ability to measure G‑V‑R improvements under the preregistered one‑repair policy.

Shared initial‑candidate design (preregistered) fixes the same initial generation for both arms to isolate repair effect; this reduces sensitivity to generator variability and can mask repair value when the generator is already accurate on the task set.
Only a single automatic repair attempt was permitted per task; iterative or human‑in‑the‑loop repair policies were not evaluated.
Automated contamination detection cannot eliminate memorization risk entirely; the preregistered contamination summary reported zero flagged pairs but residual uncertainty remains.
